problem: Object-navigation systems stop within 1-2 m of the target, leaving a gap to a manipulation-ready base pose. Position-only action-chunk policies (ACT/DP) and position-only teleoperation also cause lag, jitter and unstable contact during sustained articulated-object interaction.
motivation: Household quadruped mobile manipulation needs the base to end in a pose compatible with the interaction, and then needs smooth, stable contact along constrained trajectories (drawers, lamps, toilet lids). Static readiness criteria (reachability, orientation, clearance) do not capture the motion evolution needed during contact, and position-only demonstrations and policies lack velocity information.
key_idea: Combine MLLM chain-of-thought instruction decomposition plus a visual last-mile approach module for manipulation-ready navigation with a position-velocity-coupled teleoperation and an ACT policy that jointly predicts joint-position and joint-velocity chunks.
insight: Both navigation and manipulation gains are attributed to explicit structure. PP-CoT raises overall navigation SR from 26.67% to 60% for Qwen-3.7-Max and from 13.33% to 46.67% for Doubao. In manipulation, P-V teleoperation and the velocity/consistency losses are complementary: TONAV without P-V control reaches 53.33%, and with P-V demonstrations 80%. Baselines ACT and DP also improve with P-V demonstrations, to 46.67% and 26.67%. Caveat: only 5 trials per task, so differences are noisy.
method: Action-Velocity Teleoperation Framework (AVTF): master joint velocity is estimated by backward finite difference and clipped; the follower tracks position and velocity through an MIT-style impedance controller (kp=8, kd=0.1) at 220 Hz. Recording runs separately at 30 Hz with timestamp alignment.

Perception-Planning CoT (PP-CoT): two-stage zero-shot MLLM inference. Perception extracts the target, landmarks and free space; planning produces landmark-based navigation sub-instructions (forward, turn at landmark, approach, stop).

Adaptive Approach Module (AAM): an open-vocabulary detector initializes SAM2 tracking, and mask-median pixel plus median depth are back-projected to a 3D target point. An ego-motion-aware delayed-observation Kalman filter maintains the target state. A hybrid controller regulates the horizontal alignment error and the stand-off distance error d* (chosen from the arm workspace), with a safe stop when perception is unreliable. A pretrained diffusion policy handles coarse approach.
Action-velocity chunk policy: an ACT-style CVAE (ResNet-18, transformer with hidden dim 512, chunk size 30) takes RGB and proprioception, and two heads predict a position chunk and a velocity chunk.
Loss: L1 position loss (supervised on executed follower positions) + 0.1 velocity L1 + 0.1 motion-consistency loss (finite difference of predicted positions vs predicted velocity, dt=1/30 s) + 10 KL.
Position-only baseline protocol: data is collected with position-only commands, and at inference kd=0 removes the velocity term.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.7-Max (frozen, zero-shot PP-CoT); open-vocab detector + SAM2 + DINOv2 features + pretrained diffusion policy for AAM; ResNet-18 + ACT CVAE (trained) for manipulation
setting.training_data: Real-world teleoperated demonstrations collected with AVTF for each manipulation task (scale not stated); PP-CoT is training-free; the approach diffusion policy is pretrained
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB + depth (onboard camera), global observation image for PP-CoT, robot odometry and proprioception
setting.action_space: High-level: language navigation sub-instructions executed as base velocity commands (angular/forward) by AAM; manipulation: arm joint-position chunks (with velocity) on Piper arms

numbers_note: Custom real-world benchmarks only (15 trials per method); no standard benchmark results. Text says navigation SR is 80/60/40% for the three tasks; the Table 1 counts read 4/5, 3/5, 2/5, and the 60.00% overall equals 9/15, so the text and table disagree slightly per task.
results: On real-robot tasks TONAV reaches 60.00% navigation SR versus StreamVLN 13.33% and InternNav 26.67%. Complete manipulation reaches 80.00% versus ACT 46.67% and DP 26.67% when both use P-V demonstrations, and versus 13.33% for ACT/DP without P-V control.
limitations: Very small evaluation (5 trials per task, 3 tasks, one robot), so results have high variance and no significance testing
Navigation SR stays modest (60%), and Lower Toilet Lid is only 40%; the pipeline depends on proprietary MLLMs, with 2 stage inference at up to 120 s per stage
No tactile or force feedback; generalization to varied scene layouts and initial configurations is untested
